sentences.text: Ophthalmosaurus was a medium-sized ichthyosaur that grew to a length of 4 meters and weighed 940 kilograms.
This animal possessed a teardrop-shaped body and a crescent-shaped tail fin.
Its front flippers were more developed than its hind limbs, suggesting the front flippers steered while the tail provided propulsion.
The eyes occupied almost the entire skull space and were protected by bony plates called the scleral ring, likely to maintain eye shape against deep-water pressure.
Ophthalmosaurus is famous for its large eyes, which reached a diameter of 10.16 centimeters.
It gave birth by pushing its young out tail-first to prevent them from drowning.
Fossil skeletons of unborn young found in nearly fifty females show that litters ranged from two to eleven offspring.
The genus Ophthalmosaurus was first described by Harry Seeley in 1874.
Harry Seeley described Ophthalmosaurus in 1874, focusing on clavicular bone morphology.
There are 27 recorded fossil occurrences of Ophthalmosaurus.
The size of the eyes and scleral rings suggests Ophthalmosaurus hunted in deep, dark waters or at night when prey was active.
Calculations suggest a typical Ophthalmosaurus could remain submerged for approximately 20 minutes or more.
Assuming a conservative swimming speed of 1 m/s, Ophthalmosaurus could dive to 600 meters and return to the surface in 20 minutes.
Evidence in Ophthalmosaurus skeletons suggests it suffered from decompression sickness, possibly due to evasion tactics.
Ophthalmosaurus is classified in the class Reptilia.
It is classified in the family Ophthalmosauridae.
The genus belongs to the parent group Ophthalmosaurinae.
Ophthalmosaurus lived from the Middle Jurassic to the Late Jurassic, with possible remains from the earliest Cretaceous (Berriasian).
It lived from the Middle Jurassic to the early Late Jurassic, between 165 and 157 million years ago.
